chunks: He said: And some of our companions narrated from Abu Muhammad al-Bazzaz, who said: Amr ibn Minhal al-Qummat narrated to us from Hadid al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

He said: Indeed, Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) has two occultations; one is short and the other is long, until a person comes to you who claims that he died, prayer was performed over him, he was buried, and he shook the dust of the grave from his hand. He is a liar in that; the Successor will not die until he appoints a Successor, and only the Successor succeeds the Successor, but if someone else succeeds him, he will be blinded.
ai.seo_question: What are the two occultations of Imam Abu al-Hasan and how is the false claim of his death refuted?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* establishes the doctrine of two occultations (*al-Ghaybatan*) for Imam al-Hasan al-Askari, distinguishing between the minor and major periods. It specifically refutes the *Waqifiya* sect by asserting that the Imam does not die until he appoints his successor, thereby ensuring the continuity of divine authority (*Imamah*) without a gap in leadership.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 52 - Some of our scholars have narrated from Abu Muhammad Bazzaz that he said: Narrated to us Amr bin Minhal Qummat from Hadid Sabati from Imam Ja’far Sadiq (a.s) that he said:

Abul Hasan, Kadhim (a.s) will have two occultations: one would be short and the other lengthy. Till the time a person will come to you and report that he has participated in his funeral etc., in that case that person is definitely a liar. My successor will not die till he has fulfilled the duty of his successorship, and the matters of the successor are not taken up, except by the successor and if anyone else performed this duty, he would lose his eyesight.
